Ch18: 함정 구간 전수 보존 — 이드로(미디안 제사장·모세 장인), 십보라·게르솜(나그네)·엘리에셀(하나님의 도움) 이름 뜻, 하나님의 산 진지, 이드로의 찬양('하나님이 모든 신보다 크시다'), 번제·제사·장로들과 식사, 종일 재판(아침~밤), 이드로의 조직 개편안(하나님 경외·정직·뇌물 안 받는 유능한 자, 천부장·백부장·오십부장·십부장, 쉬운 일은 직접·어려운 일은 모세에게), 모세 수용·이드로 귀국
paragraphs: Jethro, priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law, heard all the reports of what God had done for Moses and Israel his people — the news that God had delivered Israel from Egypt. Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, had taken in Zipporah, Moses' wife, who had been sent back home, along with her two sons. One was named Gershom (Sojourner), because Moses had said, "I'm a sojourner in a foreign land"; the other's name was Eliezer (God's-Help), because "The God of my father is my help and saved me from death by Pharaoh."

Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought Moses his sons and his wife there in the wilderness, where he was camped at the mountain of God. He had sent a message ahead to Moses: "I, your father-in-law, am coming to you with your wife and two sons."

Moses went out to welcome his father-in-law. He bowed to him and kissed him. Each asked the other how things had been. Then they went into the tent. Moses told his father-in-law the whole story of what God had done to Pharaoh and Egypt for Israel's sake — all the trouble they'd run into on the journey, and how God had delivered them.

Jethro was delighted at all the good God had done for Israel in delivering them from Egyptian oppression. Jethro said, "Blessed be God, who delivered you from the power of Egypt and Pharaoh — who delivered his people from Egyptian oppression. Now I know that God is greater than all gods, because he's done this to all those who treated Israel arrogantly."
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought a Whole-Burnt-Offering and sacrifices to God. And Aaron, along with all Israel's elders, came and ate the meal with Moses' father-in-law in God's presence.

The next day Moses took his place to judge the people. People stood before him all day long, from morning to night. When Moses' father-in-law saw all he was doing for the people, he said, "What's going on here? Why are you doing all this by yourself, with everybody lined up before you from morning to night?"

Moses told his father-in-law, "Because the people come to me with questions about God. When something comes up, they come to me. I judge between a man and his neighbor, and I teach them God's laws and instructions."

Moses' father-in-law said, "This is no way to do it. You'll burn out — and the people with you. This is way too much for you; you can't do it alone. Now listen to me. Let me tell you how to do this so God will be in it with you. Be there for the people before God, but bring the hard questions to God. Your job is to teach them the rules and instructions — show them how to live, what to do. And then keep a sharp eye out for capable men — men who fear God, men of integrity, men who can't be bought — and appoint them as leaders over groups of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens. They'll handle the everyday judging among the people. They'll bring the hard cases to you, but they'll judge the routine cases themselves. They'll share your load, and that'll make it easier for you. If you work this way, you'll have the strength to carry out whatever God commands you, and the people in their settings will flourish too."

Moses listened to his father-in-law's advice and did everything he said. Moses picked capable men from all Israel and set them as leaders over the people, organized by thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens. They took over the everyday judging among the people. They brought the hard cases to Moses, but they judged the routine cases themselves. Then Moses said goodbye to his father-in-law, who went home to his own country.
title: Jethro's Advice
